description:
FILED s506f (Opus, s507 resume, 2026-10-04) from the F1 review probe (scratch/s506f/s507/f1.pl).

PROBE (perl 5.40.3):
    perl -e '$^W=5; print "$^W\n"; $^W="abc"; print "$^W\n"; $^W=undef; print "[$^W]\n"; $^W=0.5; print "$^W\n"; $^W=-1; print "$^W\n"'
    -> 1 / 0 (+ "isn't numeric" warning) / [0] / 0 / 1
    perl -e '$^W=1; { local $^W; print defined $^W ? "[$^W]" : "undef" }'  -> [0]
PCL (s506f tree): 5 / abc / [] / 0.5 / -1, and `local $^W;` -> undef.

WHY IT MATTERS LITTLE: every gate on $^W is a truth test (`warn … if $^W`), and the truth of what PCL stores
equals perl's in all but the "abc"/0.5 shapes (true in PCL, 0 in perl).  The visible difference is printing it.

SHAPE: $^W became a plain p-box in s506f (it was a raw 0 and an assignment was silently lost).  perl's shape is
SET MAGIC (mg.c: PL_dowarn from SvIV).  PCL has the mechanism — a p-magic-cell box like |$.| / |$!| (getter +
setter) — but `local $^W` binds a NEW box (p-box-for-local), so a magic cell needs its own local form (like
p-local-dot).  Cost/benefit: small; do it only together with any other $^W work (#221 warnings model).
subject: $^W stores whatever is assigned; perl's $^W is magic and stores the TRUTH of the integer value (5 -> 1, "abc" -> 0, undef -> 0, 0.5 -> 0, -1 -> 1), and `local $^W;` reads 0 in perl, undef in PCL
